slides.title: Lost the pitch? It probably wasn't just [price].
slides.lede: A lower fee might reflect a smaller scope, less senior involvement or a more comfortable commitment. The useful question is what the buyer chose instead, and why.

slides.title: Ask what they [chose instead]
slides.note: Doing nothing is still a purchasing decision. **Each alternative represents a different positioning problem.**

slides.title: What made appointing you feel like the [bigger commitment]?
slides.text: Ask what concerned them about each provider. A managing partner might focus on commercial risk, an operations director on delivery capacity, a marketing director on sector knowledge.

slides.title: What were they [willing to give up]?

cards.label: What the buyer interview found
cards.text: They accepted a narrower delivery model for direct principal access.

slides.title: Your wins show which [strengths to keep]
slides.text: Studying only failed proposals gives an incomplete picture. Successful clients reveal what created confidence and why your firm became preferable to the alternatives.
